item.title: 'Landman' season 3 shoots at familiar 'Yellowstone' filming locations owned by Taylor Sheridan
item.description: "Landman" season 3 is now filming at Taylor Sheridan's Bosque Ranch and 6666 Ranch, locations fans recognize from "Yellowstone" and "Lioness."
item.content:encoded:
"Landman" viewers might recognize a familiar spot in season three.

The hit series created by Taylor Sheridan focuses on the oil business, and stars Billy Bob Thornton at Tommy Norris. He's joined in the cast by Ali Larter, Sam Elliott, Michelle Randolph, Kayla Wallace, Jacob Lofland and Demi Moore.

The first two seasons dominated the entertainment sphere, and were exactly what Sheridan fans have come to expect from the "Yellowstone" creator.

TAYLOR SHERIDAN'S LANDMAN FACES LENGTHY WAIT AS SEASON 3 PRODUCTION TIMELINE REVEALED

Season two ended in January 2026, and fans are gearing up for season three, which is expected in 2027.

While there's no exact release date for season three, fans recently received a positive update.....that features a very recognizable location.

TAYLOR SHERIDAN'S 'LANDMAN' SEASON 3 IS FILMING AT TCU IN FORT WORTH WITH 30 CHEERLEADERS ON SET

Singer Clayton Q recently shared on Instagram that season three of "Landman" is filming at Bosque Ranch in Weatherford, Texas.

The ranch is owned by Sheridan, and fans of his work will recognize it for one simple reason:

It appeared in several of his biggest hits.

Filming occurred at Bosque Ranch for "Yellowstone," "Lawmen: Bass Reeves" and "Lioness." It won't be the only spot fans of Sheridan's work recognize in season three.

TAYLOR SHERIDAN TAKES SWIPE AT LOS ANGELES AFTER BUILDING TV EMPIRE FROM TEXAS

Clayton Q also revealed "Landman" also is shooting at Sheridan's 6666 Ranch. The massive ranch also appeared in "Yellowstone."

It's not clear as of right now what role the locations will play in season three of the hit series with Billy Bob Thornton, and I'm sure fans are eager to find out.

Season three of "Landman" has no official release date as of publication, but it is highly likely new episodes will drop at some point in 2027. Have a fun theory for where things go next? Let me know at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

item.title: Trump says he 'can't imagine' Democrats will impeach him a third time
item.description: President Donald Trump told "60 Minutes" that he doubts Democrats will impeach him a third time despite a past history of animosity towards each other.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump sat down with CBS News' "60 Minutes" on Sunday and expressed doubts that Democrats will attempt to impeach him a third time once they retake Congress in January.

Trump spoke with correspondent Ross Douthat for his first sit-down interview since the midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party made historic gains. 

Despite his past conflicts with the Democratic Party, Trump told Douthat that he could "very easily" make a deal with Democrats, citing his first term as an example.

"Well, I did it for four years," Trump said. "You know ... what they did with me was, there's never been [such] weaponization. They impeached me twice. And there are those that say that worked out to my advantage."

TRUMP CONGRATULATES DEMOCRATS AFTER DOMINANT MIDTERMS, SAYS HE LOOKS FORWARD TO WORKING WITH THEM

"Do you think they'll impeach you again?" Douthat asked.

"I can't imagine it, you know?" Trump responded. "Look, what have I done? I've had the best two years in the history of the presidency."

Trump's comments come after several Democratic figures have called for investigations and subpoenas against members of the Trump administration.

However, other Democratic Party members, including former Vice President Kamala Harris, have discouraged the incoming Congress from focusing too much on impeaching the president.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

Although Trump expressed a willingness to work with the Democratic Congress in the present, he admitted to Douthat that, even "before the judgment throne of God," he doubted that he could forgive some of his enemies, like former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi or former FBI Director James Comey.

Comey's team did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Pelosi's office also did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 

"I found them to be extremely dishonest people, very bad people, very bad for our country. I love our country far more than I can love people and people like that," Trump said.

He added, "I think they were very bad people and I dislike, I can use the word 'hate,' I do hate some of my enemies. I think they're ... they've been terrible. Look what they've put me through, the weaponization."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Douthat repeatedly asked Trump whether he could find it in his heart to forgive his enemies, but Trump remained firm in his answer.

"I probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies, and I always will," Trump said.

During Trump's first term, he was impeached by the House in 2019 but was acquitted by the Senate months later. After the Jan. 6 Capitol riots, the president was impeached again, but was ultimately acquitted by the Senate.

item.title: Hilary Duff says child stardom left ‘scars from the past’: ‘People don’t survive that’
item.description: Hilary Duff opened up about how she had to confront "scars from the past" after returning to the stage for her "Lucky Me Tour" following 20 years away.
item.content:encoded:
Hilary Duff is opening up about the "scars from the past" she had to confront as a former child star.

In a recent interview with Billboard, the 39-year-old actress and singer, who rose to fame at 14 when she starred in the hit Disney Channel series "Lizzie McGuire," reflected on the lasting effects of childhood stardom as she discussed her return to music after more than a decade.

In February, Duff released "Luck … Or Something," her first studio album since 2015's "Breathe In. Breathe Out." The album debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200 chart. In June, Duff launched the "Lucky Me Tour," her first major tour in nearly two decades.

BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA

Before launching her tour, Duff gave an intimate performance for friends and family in Los Angeles in January. She told Billboard that she was so nervous during the show that her hand shook as she held the microphone.

The "Younger" star recalled that after the performance, her son, Luca, told her he was proud of her for returning to the stage despite her fears.

"That stuck with me, because it is scary, and I'm used to being so tough and strong," she said. "This industry really makes you very rough around the edges, where you're like, 'I've got to handle this, so I just will.'"

"But it was scary to step onstage after 20 years and figure out my identity, and how I move my body and what I'm taking from my old persona and adding to who I am now," Duff continued. "It was a complicated thing to do, and I had to get over quite a few scars from the past."

FORMER DISNEY STAR DYLAN SPROUSE SAYS ACTING AS A KID WAS ‘CHILD LABOR’

Although she stepped away from music for more than a decade, Duff said some of the habits she developed during her years as a child star have been difficult to shake.

According to Billboard, Duff repeatedly referred to herself as a "Disney dog" during the interview, describing an ingrained impulse to "say yes and to go, go, go."

DOLLY PARTON DEFIED COUNTRY MUSIC'S EXPECTATIONS FOR WOMEN AND BUILT A CAREER ON HER OWN TERMS: EXPERTS

Duff also said returning to music as an adult has allowed her to take greater control of her career than she had as a child star.

"It was wonderful building this on my terms," she said. "I don't mean that negatively in regard to how anything was handled in the past, because I was a child in the past. I wasn't muted, and I got to make decisions, but people made a lot of decisions for me because I didn't care or know enough to be like, 'Here's how I want this.'"

DISNEY ALUM CHRISTY CARLSON ROMANO RIPS HOLLYWOOD FOR FAILING CHILD STARS AFTER HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S DEATH

Duff also acknowledged that she continues to grapple with the experience of becoming famous at a young age.

"I've had a great career and I feel really lucky," she said. "I also am a child star, and that's a really hard thing to wrestle with as an adult. People don't survive that."

'AMERICAN IDOL' STAR JUSTIN GUARINI ENDURED DARK SPIRAL AFTER HOLLYWOOD DREAM COLLAPSED

"The fact that I've been able to survive and that I get to have this moment … I get to send love to grown-up Hilary and be like, 'You did it!' and also send love to little Hilary and be like, 'Hey, we're still here. Look at what we did.'"

The "Lucky Me Tour" kicked off on June 21 in West Palm Beach, Florida, and included stops at Madison Square Garden in New York City and the Kia Forum in Inglewood, California, before heading to Europe, Australia and New Zealand. Due to strong demand, Duff extended the tour through 2027 with 32 additional dates across Europe, Latin America and the U.S.

Duff told Billboard that reconnecting with longtime fans has helped her heal some of the wounds left by childhood fame. She said she now makes a point of thanking fans during her concerts for "letting me grow up."

"I understand fans hold me in this sweet capsule in their heart that holds a time in their life that was tender and uncomplicated," Duff said.

'LITTLE HOUSE ON THE PRAIRIE' STAR SAYS CHILD ACTORS GET 'DROPPED' AFTER HOLLYWOOD FAME FADES

"But putting out a very honest and exposed record and them digesting and accepting it and being like, 'Me Too' — that was very healing for me," she continued. "It showed me that they don't just care about me as the person they hold in that capsule, they care about me now as well."

item.title: Devils to sit star goalie vs his former team over 'win probability,' leaving NHL fans bewildered
item.description: Devils GM Sunny Mehta cited "expected win probability" in benching Connor Hellebuyck for his return to Winnipeg, leaving fans baffled by the move.
item.content:encoded:
The New Jersey Devils emerged as one of the best teams in the NHL this season and beefed up their roster when they acquired goaltender Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets.

The Devils shut out the Toronto Maple Leafs on Sunday, increasing the anticipation for a matchup on Tuesday between New Jersey and Winnipeg in Canada. However, general manager Sunny Mehta shut down the possibility of Hellebuyck playing and gave a bizarre reason as to why.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"This has been an organizational decision for us that we’ve debated at length," Mehta said. "Connor Hellebuyck was adamant that he felt a duty to play on Tuesday in Winnipeg. However, in our estimation, playing in this game would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability.

"Even though Connor isn’t playing, at his request, we will coordinate a media availability after Tuesday’s morning skate at Canada Life Centre."

Hellebuyck made 23 saves against Toronto in the 4-0 victory and will have a day of rest in between games. Instead, Jake Allen will likely get the nod in between the pipes because of a "reduction in our expected win probability."

As the kids say these days, "the math ain’t mathin’."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Fans were just as confused by the statement.

Hellebuyck said it would have been nice to play in Winnipeg again after the Jets traded him to the Devils last month for Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws and a 2029 second-round draft pick.

"I know there’s a pretty sour taste in Winnipeg," Hellebuyck said. "But I can only speak to my memories and my cherished moments in the city. I’ve loved every part of my career there. However, I’m perceived, I’m going to choose love."

New Jersey is 13-5 this season, sitting just four points (26) behind the Carolina Hurricanes (30) for first place in the Metropolitan Division. The Boston Bruins are the only other team that have more points (27) than the Devils.

Hellebuyck has yet to lose as a goaltender for New Jersey. He has a 1.96 goals against average and makes 91.3% of his saves.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: AG Blanche clashes with anchor asking whether it's his 'job' to defend the Trump administration
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche clashed with CNN's Dana Bash over his vow to defend the Trump administration against recent Democratic congressional threats.
item.content:encoded:
Attorney General Todd Blanche repeatedly clashed with CNN host Dana Bash Sunday after explaining how he and the Department of Justice will respond to recent Democratic threats to investigate the Trump administration.

Since the Democratic Party's midterm election sweep, several prominent Democrats have used the opportunity to threaten legal action against President Donald Trump and members of his Cabinet. Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., who is poised to lead the House Oversight Committee, posted "lawyer up" in response to the midterm wins, as well as the news that Stephen Miller would be promoted to White House chief of staff.

Blanche defended Miller in an X post, writing that the Attorney General of the United States and the Department of Justice would defend the White House chief of staff, leading the "State of the Union" host to ask whether his job is focused on Trump Cabinet members.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

"Do you see it as your job as attorney general to represent anyone in the administration being investigated by Congress?" Bash said.

"Wait, do I see it as my job?" Blanche responded. "The Constitution sees it as my job. Just in every administration, the Department of Justice represents members of the executive who are brought in front of Congress. So, there is nothing unique to me saying that. Every attorney general in history represents members of the administration."

"And this idea that Congressman Garcia comes out and says, 'Oh, no, no. Stephen Miller needs his own personal lawyer.' I would suggest he read the Constitution," he continued. "If he doesn't have a copy, I can arrange to send him one. But the Constitution absolutely protects members of the executive, and I am the attorney general, and as that, like I do every day, we represent members of the administration who go in front of Congress. That's nothing unique to me."

DEMS PIVOT FROM ‘AFFORDABILITY’ PITCH TO DHS PROBE THREATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS

During the interview, Bash argued that Congress has an oversight role and asked whether Blanche was concerned about that.

"No, no, no," Blanche said. "They have a very unique role in oversight, I agree. Have you been listening to the rhetoric the past couple of days? You honestly think that all they’re doing is talking about their oversight obligations, when they’re talking about going after basically every member of the Cabinet? They’re talking about impeachments. They’re talking about going after companies, private companies, who happen to have made investments in this country over the past couple years. That is not oversight. I welcome oversight. Oversight is exactly something they should be doing."

"So are you saying that you are going to investigate them?" Bash said, referencing Trump's recent Truth Social post encouraging an investigation against Democrats. "And what you just described, is there a crime there?"

TODD BLANCHE CHALLENGES DANA BASH FOR ONLY CITING PART OF CONSTITUTION DURING HEATED ELECTION CLASH

Blanche answered that depending on what's said, there "could be" an investigation against some Democrats regarding their rhetoric against Trump. Blanche answered with a reference to recent remarks by Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., about hoping to discourage young conservatives from working in the government.

"You have free speech in this country. You are allowed to be critical of President Trump, of me, of this administration," Blanche said. "But when the threats become so vile and so dangerous that you are telling people in college that they better be careful if they want to work in the Trump administration because somebody will come after them, at some point you have to draw the line."

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House, the Department of Justice and Garcia's office for comment.

item.title: Mysterious blood-soaked relic linked to history's most beloved saint, St Francis of Assisi, goes on display
item.description: An 800-year-old blood relic from St. Francis of Assissi is now on display in San Francisco, California, marking the first time the sacred artifact has left Italy.
item.content:encoded:
Christians visiting San Francisco have a rare opportunity to see an 800-year-old relic believed to contain the blood of one of history's most beloved saints, St. Francis of Assisi — marking the first time the artifact has left Italy.

The relics of the saint are currently on display at the Cathedral of St. Mary of the Assumption until Nov. 28. 

The display commemorates the 800th anniversary of the death of Francis, who lived from approximately 1181 to 1226.

LOST CITY IN AREA TIED TO BIBLICAL EXODUS MAY HAVE FINALLY BEEN DISCOVERED IN EGYPT

The saint is best known for founding the Franciscan Order, as well as for being the patron saint of animals.

The exhibition includes a painted panel of the saint dating to around 1290 — but the crown jewel of the display is the Bandage Relic of the Stigmata of Saint Francis of Assisi, a centuries-old cloth believed to contain his blood.

Pictures of the relic on display show that the blood on the bandage still appears intensely red, even 800 years later.

The relics' arrival in San Francisco carries particular significance because the city was named after St. Francis, said Candida Moss, the Edward Cadbury professor of theology at the University of Birmingham.

SACRED PAGES OF 1,000-YEAR-OLD GOSPEL REVEAL ANCIENT DNA SCIENTISTS NEVER EXPECTED

"People love St. Francis, but Francis isn't just venerated by Catholics," Moss told Fox News Digital, noting that he is also revered by Orthodox Christians, Anglicans and Lutherans.

"I think this will become temporarily a pilgrimage site," she added.

Moss said St. Francis' enduring popularity stems from his extraordinary transformation from a wealthy young man to someone who devoted his life to serving the poor.

"He starts off just like everyone else. He wanted to be a knight," she said. "And then he changes his life. He ministers to the poor. He has all of these stories about him preaching to birds."

ANCIENT CHRISTIAN AMULET UNEARTHED AFTER 1,500 YEARS MAY HOLD BIBLICAL SECRET

"These are all really endearing stories about a man devoted to God," added Moss.

The bloodstained bandages are tied to another defining moment in St. Francis' life, when he reportedly experienced a vision of a seraph, a six-winged angel, and received the stigmata — wounds resembling those suffered by Jesus Christ during the crucifixion.

"He then has these wounds for the rest of his life that link him on a spiritual level to Christ," Moss said.

"And so there are so many elements of this story, the miraculous, the sentimental, the relatable, that I think make Francis one of the most popular medieval saints, if not the most popular medieval saint."

LOST PAGES WITH 'GHOST' TEXT RECOVERED FROM ONE OF THE WORLD'S MOST IMPORTANT NEW TESTAMENT MANUSCRIPTS

The exhibition also raises questions about how centuries-old religious relics are preserved and authenticated, Moss said.

While St. Francis' relics have a documented chain of custody dating back to the monastery where he died, Moss said some objects previously attributed to the saint have turned out to be inauthentic.

One example is a tunic once believed to have belonged to St. Francis that was housed in Florence. 

Carbon dating revealed that the garment was from about 150 years after his lifetime.

Moss suggested the garment was likely a "pious forgery" that had been mistakenly identified as a relic.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Although some of St. Francis' other relics have been carbon-dated to the appropriate historical period, the bloodstained bandage currently on display has not undergone such testing, according to Moss.

The reason the blood on the centuries-old bandage still appears red remains unclear.

"Now, for religious people, the explanation might be [that] this is miraculous in some way," Moss said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"But there has been no scrutiny of this particular relic, which is the most important of the Francis relics," she added. "So we can't really say for certain why it is that it seems so well-preserved."

Despite the unanswered questions about the relic's preservation, Moss emphasized the rarity of the exhibition and its importance to church history.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I think [this] is a really singular opportunity to come into contact with really high-status relics," she said.

"You can't acquire anything like this," she said. 

"You couldn't buy it on eBay, because it is against church protocols to buy this. And this is the first time that these relics have left Italy."

Moss added, "This is a really important part of church history, and it's worth seeing for yourself."

item.title: MATT CALKINS: Democrats' push to overturn girls' sports vote shows they don't actually care about democracy
item.description: Kamala Harris made democracy a campaign theme, but Washington Democrats now seek to overturn Initiative 638 after voters backed girls sports separation.
item.content:encoded:
There is no official scorecard on this one, but if there is one word I've heard more than any other from Democratic politicians over the past several years, it might be "democracy."

Kamala Harris repeatedly made "democracy is on the ballot" a central theme of her presidential campaign. California Gov. Gavin Newsom declared that "democracy is under assault across this nation." House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries promised that "we are going to fight for our democracy, fight for the rule of law, and fight for the Constitution against those who want to turn back the clock."

JACKSON THOMPSON: WASHINGTON STATE DEMOCRATIC PARTY CALLS GIRLS' SPORTS INITIATIVE UNCONSTITUTIONAL

These are three examples from a potential list of 3,000. One question, though: Why does democracy stop mattering once these Democratic politicians don't get what they want?

In this case, I'm referring specifically to the passing of Washington state's Initiative 638, which would enforce the separation of boys and girls in K-12 sports if it goes into effect. The reason I used "if" is because there are a lot of Democrats in Washington hellbent on overturning the will of the people.

To be clear, this was not a tight race. The AP called it when the "yes" side of I-638 held a 13% lead with 88 percent of the votes counted. But almost immediately, Democrats decided democracy wasn't a necessity so much as an inconvenience.

It started with Rep. Pramila Jayapal, who spoke openly about overturning the initiatives at an election-night gathering before the results were even final.

"We are going to take our state back," Jayapal said. "We're going to start planning for how we overturn these bad initiatives and how we go back to loving everyone with gender inclusivity the way we have for decades."

It continued with Washington State Democratic Party Chair Shasti Conrad, who made clear two days later that the election results weren't going to settle the issue.

"While this result is incredibly disheartening, voters in Washington and across the nation rejected anti-trans candidates up and down the ballot," Conrad said in a statement last Thursday. "The fight over I-638 is just beginning. We believe this initiative is unconstitutional on its face and support organizations planning to challenge it in court."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

One of those organizations is Gender Justice League, a Seattle-based LGBTQ advocacy group whose executive director, Danni Askini, told KUOW that it was exploring legal options to challenge the initiative.

"We are having active conversations with our partners and also evaluating what legal options are available to us," Askini said. "If there is an avenue, we will challenge this ballot measure in court on behalf of our members and our community and trans youth."

There was even a writer named Robert Cruickshank, who penned an essay for The Bulletin in Seattle comparing I-638 to California's Proposition 8, which banned same-sex marriage in the Golden State in 2008. Cruickshank laid out a two-pronged strategy for overturning I-638: challenging it in court while simultaneously pursuing a political effort to repeal it.

For one, protecting girls from the athletically superior sex in sports is not the same as denying gay people the right to wed. The latter does not have a victim. But all these examples highlight that, to Democrats, democracy doesn't die in darkness — it dies in broad daylight when the wrong side wins.

WASHINGTON STATE'S HIGH SCHOOL SPORTS LEAGUE PUTS ONUS FOR TRANS ATHLETE CONTROVERSY ON STATE LAWS

None of this is to say that legal challenges to ballot measures are inherently illegitimate. In fact, they are a fundamental part of our constitutional framework. It's just funny that when a vote goes one way for the Democrats, it's "the people have spoken," and when it goes another way, it's "the people have spoken out of turn."

I was at the Washington state cross country finals Saturday, where a boy who switched to the girls' team midseason was competing. Several girls voiced their relief that they wouldn't have to deal with this issue again next season.

Democratic leaders have been ignoring those girls' voices all year. Seems they're ignoring the people who voted in their favor, too.

Cincinnati made a habit of getting off to slow starts and had to rally from 13-point deficits in each of the past two weeks, including needing overtime to beat the lowly Titans. After allowing the Falcons to score a touchdown on their first drive, the Bengals dominated in Spain. It was another come-from-behind victory, but this one wasn't a sweat.

Cincinnati answered with four straight scoring drives to take a 24-10 lead into halftime. Atlanta never got closer than a 7-point deficit in the second half, and when they did cut it to one score, Cincinnati immediately answered with another touchdown. If the Bengals defense can keep playing like it did on Sunday, there's little that can be done to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

Takeaway: A win is a win.

We shouldn't pretend the New York Giants are a great football team, but they are 5-2-1 on the year and comfortably in first place in the NFC East. Hiring Super Bowl-winning coach John Harbaugh after Baltimore fired him already looks like a home run for New York. The Giants have dealt with a ton of injuries, including to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, but they've managed to keep the season on track.

Takeaway: Sean Payton owes NFL referees a fruit basket or something.

The Denver Broncos have won two games this season thanks in large part to controversial calls that benefitted them. On Sunday, officials flagged the Panthers 13 times for 119 yards, including several third-down penalties that kept Denver drives alive. That's not to say they were all bad calls, but it definitely seemed like the Broncos got the better side of the yellow markers.

Officials also allowed Payton to challenge an incompletion after Carolina had already run another play, saying he had thrown the flag before the snap. The review gave Denver the ball on Devon Key's interception. Despite all that, they still almost blew a 12-point lead with less than 6 minutes remaining, but got a huge strip-sack from Nik Bonitto to seal the win.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Takeaway: Don't look now, but the "superteam" is finally over .500.

Perhaps no team in the NFL has been hurt by injuries more than the Rams, but for the first time this season, they have more wins than losses. It wasn't pretty, as most of their games haven't been, but Los Angeles managed to hang on to win their third straight game after a 2-4 start. Sean McVay has brought the Rams back from slow starts before, and they are starting to get healthy, with Myles Garrett returning on Sunday. They still don't look like the team that everyone thought was definitely going to win the Super Bowl, but they probably aren't a team that opponents are going to want to face in January.

Takeaway: Kansas City did what it was supposed to do.

When a team as good as the Chiefs hosts a team as bad as the Jets, they're supposed to run them out of the building. And that's exactly what Kansas City did. The Chiefs outscored the Jets 21-0 in the second half and cruised to a victory. They also survived an injury scare involving Patrick Mahomes' right arm. Mahomes was shaken up but returned for Kansas City's next possession. His health is worth monitoring because an injury to Mahomes is about the only thing that could derail Kansas City's hopes for a fourth Super Bowl title in eight seasons.

Takeaway: The Lions won a game they should have won, so good for them.

Detroit didn't exactly put on an offensive clinic, but it didn't need to against the Dolphins. Jake Bates kicked four field goals, Jahmyr Gibbs scored the game's only touchdown and the Lions defense kept Miami out of the end zone. The Lions have now won four straight and sit at 6-2, which matters a lot more than this one win. Beating the 1-7 Dolphins isn't going to convince anyone of anything they didn't already think about Detroit, but losing to them certainly would have.

Takeaway: Neither of these teams is very good.

The Cowboys and Colts turned in one of the most entertaining games of Week 9. Indianapolis kicked a go-ahead 50-yard field goal with 1:37 left, only for Dallas to respond with a game-winning touchdown less than 30 seconds later. But don't mistake exciting and entertaining for... good. The Colts have basically punted on the season, and the Cowboys still needed a late touchdown to beat them. The game featured 23 penalties and four turnovers combined, with Dallas racking up an unconscionable 153 penalty yards. Miraculously, the Cowboys are still very much alive in the NFC East, but they aren't a very good team.

Takeaway: Shedeur Sanders did enough to create a QB controversy in Cleveland.

For much of Sunday's game, Sanders looked a lot like Deshaun Watson (with regard to his play, not the ... other stuff). His 297 yards and two touchdowns look better than his actual performance, and his receivers deserve plenty of credit for that. But his 30-yard strike to Jerry Jeudy while taking a huge hit from Chase Young helped set up the game-tying field goal and was probably the best throw by a Browns quarterback this season.

SHEDEUR SANDERS MAKES CASE TO REPLACE DESHAUN WATSON AFTER BROWNS' OVERTIME LOSS TO SAINTS

Sanders then helped put Cleveland in position to win in overtime before a failed two-point attempt ended it. Watson hasn't exactly done enough to cement his status as the starter. If the Browns are going to get uneven quarterback play no matter who starts, why not let the 24-year-old develop through it?

Takeaway: Someone is going to have to get fired.

The obvious choice is offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, but the Chargers' problems run deeper than just McDaniel (although he certainly isn't helping). Los Angeles went 12 full quarters (the equivalent of three NFL games) without scoring an offensive touchdown before finally breaking through. By then, they already trailed 38-9 in the fourth quarter.

That's the real problem: Los Angeles isn't even competitive at this point. This was their third straight loss by at least 15 points, and five of their eight losses have been by double digits. Disaster and dumpster fire don't even fully encapsulate the mess that the Chargers are right now. The bigger question is whether the Chargers use what's likely to be a top-five pick in the NFL Draft on a quarterback to replace Justin Herbert.

Takeaway: Brock Purdy should be the NFL MVP favorite.

Purdy isn't the most talented or flashiest player in the league, but what he's doing this season can't be overstated. The 49ers have been decimated at the wide receiver position, with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel currently out, Brandon Aiyuk off doing who knows what, and Ricky Pearsall and Christian Kirk on IR. Purdy has completed 69% of his passes and is on pace to throw for over 4,000 yards this season. Jordan Watkins, who entered Sunday with eight career catches, led the team with 86 receiving yards and a touchdown. It almost doesn't matter who suits up at receiver for San Francisco; if he's wearing a 49ers jersey, Purdy is going to find a way to get him the ball and put points on the board.

Takeaway: There's not a lot to take away from this game.

The Cardinals stink, but we already knew that. The Seahawks are probably good, but we still don't really know. Drew Lock started in place of Sam Darnold, so we didn't learn much about Seattle's offense. And shutting down a Gardner Minshew-led Arizona offense doesn't tell us much about a defense that allowed 34 points to the Bears one week after holding the Chiefs to three. Seattle has been up and down following its Super Bowl championship, but this game ultimately didn't answer any real questions. Those are going to be answered on Nov. 29, when the Seahawks travel to San Francisco to face the NFC West-leading 49ers.

Takeaway: I'm trying not to overreact, but my goodness, the Packers look incredible.

This isn't the same Patriots team that reached the Super Bowl last season, and it certainly isn't the same Drake Maye who finished second in NFL MVP voting. That being said, New England isn't that bad. Yet Green Bay made New England's defense look like it was playing with nine players. And the Packers defense forced four turnovers, including three interceptions of Maye.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Since Atlanta embarrassed Green Bay in Week 3, the Packers are 5-1, and their only loss came in a game they really should have won at Detroit. They have some big games coming up against the Vikings and Rams, and we're going to find out if this team is really the Super Bowl contender it has looked like over the past six games.

Takeaway: NFL fans got the full Caleb Williams experience on Sunday Night Football.

Williams is probably the most physically gifted quarterback in the NFL right now and arguably the most talented thrower of the football in the world. But questions about his decision-making remain. For the first 21 minutes of Sunday Night Football, Williams looked like the best quarterback in the NFL. He was making throws that no one else in the league could make, firing pass after pass off platform and hitting his receivers in stride.

But the problem with guys like Williams, who are capable of making every throw, is that they start to think they WILL make every throw. He started forcing the ball, throwing interceptions on consecutive passes in the second quarter. He threw a third pick on the team's final drive of the first half and added another in the third quarter.

Williams completed 11 of his first 16 passes for 150 yards and two touchdowns. His next 16 attempts produced just seven completions, 73 yards and four interceptions. Fortunately for Williams and the Bears, Tampa Bay managed just three points off his four interceptions, and Baker Mayfield threw two picks of his own, including a pick-six.

The tools are all there, but if the Bears are going to be true Super Bowl contenders, Williams has to clean up the mistakes. Quickly.

item.title: Rubio defends Trump's Iran war as not 'necessarily popular, but necessary'
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Trump's Iran war as "necessary" to prevent a nuclear weapon, even as he ties it to Republican midterm losses.
item.content:encoded:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended President Donald Trump's decision to launch the war on Iran, saying it was "necessary" to prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

Rubio admitted that the war was not "necessarily popular," acknowledging the war's impact on the Republicans' midterm election losses last week. Rubio made the statement in response to questions about Vice President JD Vance's statement last week that also pinned the losses on the war.

Rubio said Trump was responding to a "very real threat" when he launched the war earlier this year.

VANCE'S SCATHING IRAN WAR POSTMORTEM PUTS POTENTIAL 2028 GOP SHOWDOWN IN FOCUS: 'EVERYONE KNOWS WHY'

"He addressed it even though oftentimes the right thing to do for the country — confronting difficult challenges for the security of our country — doing it isn’t necessarily popular, but necessary," Rubio said.

Trump himself has made no apologies for the war, stating repeatedly since Election Day that he had no choice but to intervene in Iran's nuclear program.

TRUMP SAYS HE DOESN’T DISAGREE WITH VANCE THAT IRAN WAR FUELED GOP LOSSES

"I can tell you if I had it to do again, this historically — for history — will go down as one of the best things we ever did," Trump told reporters on Sunday. "Because if they ever had a nuclear weapon, they would blow up the world."

Trump nevertheless told "60 Minutes" in an interview this weekend that he is not currently looking to escalate the conflict.

IRANIAN NEGOTIATORS KICKED OUT OF US AS TALKS STALL, TRUMP LAYS OUT 'POSSIBLE' TIMELINE FOR MORE STRIKES

The U.S. and Iran are engaged in talks, but Rubio says they are making little progress.

"I wouldn’t say we’re at the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio said. "Right now, it hasn’t been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic."

TRUMP ADMIN THREATENS IRAN WITH 'CONSEQUENCES' AS ALLIES CONVENE AMID THREATS OF POST-ELECTION ESCALATION

Iran lifted its self-imposed ballistic missile-range limit and threatened to unleash new, homegrown weapons on Sunday within hours of the U.S. military launching a new task force aimed at choking off Tehran's weapons shipments and illicit trade on Nov. 7.

Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi confirmed that Iran was now abandoning its previous 2,000-kilometer, or roughly 1,240-mile, ballistic missile-range restriction.

"That restriction has been lifted for us," Mohebbi clarified in the wake of the task force announcement.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: NBC skips national anthem on 'Sunday Night Football' from Soldier Field on Veterans Day week
item.description: NBC's Sunday Night Football skipped the national anthem at Soldier Field during the NFL's Salute to Service week, and NBC executives mum on decision.
item.content:encoded:
NBC's "Sunday Night Football" broadcast is often the highest-rated show on television, and the lead up to the game before kickoff more or less marks the beginning of the broadcast so it was noticeable when Sunday night's broadcast skipped the national anthem.

... On a week the NFL is memorializing its Salute To Service campaign.

... Three days shy of Veterans Day.

... Before a game played at Chicago's Soldier Field.

FOX SPORTS TO HONOR MILITARY AHEAD OF VETERANS DAY WITH TWO-DAY SALUTE DURING COLLEGE FOOTBALL, NFL COVERAGE

Talk about missing the plot.

All audiences saw after NBC did its booth introduction talk between analyst Cris Collinsworth and play-by-play man Noah Eagle was a pregame interview with Bears quarterback Caleb Williams before viewers saw an aerial view of the field during which flag bearers were carrying a folded field-sized American flag back into one of the stadium's tunnels.

NBC'S MIKE TIRICO SIDELINED BY HEALTH ISSUE AHEAD OF BEARS VS. BUCCANEERS ON SUNDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL

OutKick contacted NBC executive vice president of communications Greg Hughes and senior vice president of communications Chris McCloskey to ask why the national anthem was omitted from the broadcast.

Neither executive had responded as of publication.

NBC did cover the trade of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears. It did broadcast the "show anthem" featuring Carrie Underwood.

Viewers, meanwhile, have apparently noticed "The Star-Spangled Banner's" absence – at least some on social media.

The decision to broadcast the national anthem is not generally made by the NFL. It is not a club decision. It is a network decision.

So this is apparently an editorial decision at NBC.

One must note that this is not the first national anthem misstep prior to a Bears game this season.

CALEB WILLIAMS, LIMITED BY A HAMSTRING INJURY, SEEN CASUALLY PACING BEARS SIDELINE DURING NATIONAL ANTHEM

On September 28, the Bears hosted a Mariachi Herencia de Mexico to perform the national anthem on ESPN/ABC's Monday Night Football.

What was not met with mixed reaction was injured Bears quarterback Caleb Williams shown pacing along the sideline while the anthem was being played.

item.title: 6-minute daily habit could help Ozempic users preserve muscle, expert says
item.description: Gary Brecka says just six minutes of daily resistance training can help protect lean body mass during Ozempic and Wegovy weight loss journeys.
item.content:encoded:
As more Americans turn to popular GLP-1 medications such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound to lose weight or manage diabetes, there is a growing focus on protecting muscle as pounds are shed.

The concern comes as 11% of U.S. adults report taking these drugs for weight loss, up from 3% in 2024, according to Gallup.

Lean mass, which includes muscle and other tissues, accounts for roughly a quarter to a third of the weight lost with these obesity treatments, research suggests.

4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS

Gary Brecka, a biologist and longevity expert in Miami, Florida, shared with Fox News Digital his simple strategy for helping people preserve muscle — starting with just six minutes of exercise a day.

"GLP-1s can be life-saving for people, especially for people who are morbidly obese or have type 2 diabetes, but they can also be fascinating shifts in someone's trajectory of their wellness journey," he said.

"What's critically important for people who embark on a GLP-1 journey is to make sure that they are mitigating the lean body-mass loss."

Brecka emphasized that weight loss is not exclusively fat loss.

OZEMPIC USERS MAY BE MAKING A MAJOR WEIGHT-LOSS MISTAKE, NEW STUDY SUGGESTS

"When most people say, ‘I want to lose weight,’ what they're really saying is, ‘I want to lose fat,’" he said. "But with GLP-1s, you have a double-edged sword. About 20% to 40% of the weight that you lose is what we call lean body mass."

Lean body mass includes not only muscle, but also water, organs, blood and connective tissues, such as tendons and ligaments. Brecka emphasized that preserving lean tissue should be a priority during treatment.

Maintaining strength also helps people remain independent as they age, supporting everyday activities such as bathing, dressing and walking.

"The more that we can maintain control and dominion over those, the more independent we can be," Brecka said.

WEEKLY WEIGHTLIFTING SWEET SPOT MAY BE LINKED TO LONGER LIFE, STUDY FINDS

Challenging the body through exercise encourages it to adapt and grow stronger, Brecka said.

"But when it comes to a GLP-1 journey, you've got to give up a little bit of that comfort to reach your goals," he said.

Brecka recommends starting with six minutes of resistance exercise each day.

"People think of weight-training or resistance training as something they've got to dedicate 60 to 90 minutes to every day, and therefore they think they don't have enough time in their day," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

It’s also important to pair the strength training with adequate protein to help preserve muscle during weight loss.

Protein provides amino acids that help the body build and maintain muscle and other tissues, including tendons, ligaments and cartilage, Brecka said.

Busy people who don’t have time for lengthy gym sessions can fit resistance training into their day by "snacking" on exercise, the longevity expert said.

Brecka suggested simple exercises such as holding a plank with the knees on the floor, progressing to a full plank as strength allows, or doing body-weight squats and abdominal crunches.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

He also recommended resistance exercises using dumbbells or barbells, preferably moving through a full range of motion. One example is a goblet squat, which involves holding a dumbbell near the chest while squatting and standing.

"You don't have to lift like a bodybuilder to mitigate lean body mass loss," he said. "All you have to do is provide resistance for these tissues so that your body doesn't begin to reabsorb them while you're on this GLP-1 journey."

In terms of frequency, Brecka said exercise should be "non-negotiable" as a daily practice. He recommends a minimum of three days of resistance training and a minimum of three days of cardiovascular training.

"Cardiovascular training can be as simple as walking outside, taking your dog for a 20-minute walk," he said, adding that a weighted vest can make the same walk more challenging by increasing the load the body carries.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"If you're going to an airport, skip the moving walkway, skip the escalator, just take the steps," Brecka suggested. "There are simple things that you can do every single day … that have a dramatic impact on your body's ability to rebuild these tissues."

"These small choices throughout our lifetime are what build resilience for the decades ahead."

Protein does more than just support muscle, according to Brecka. 

Whether protein comes from chicken, beef or plant-based foods, the body breaks it down into amino acids that help build and repair muscle and other tissues, including tendons, ligaments and cartilage.

"Protein is important for so many more things than just muscle and the physical things that we see on the outside," Brecka said. "It's also responsible for building these lean body mass structures."

Current federal dietary guidelines recommend 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily.

A joint advisory on GLP-1 treatment discusses the same range during active weight loss, while emphasizing that targets should be tailored to the individual.

Brecka also urged patients to pay attention to declining energy or exercise performance, such as finding a previously easy flight of stairs suddenly difficult, and discuss those changes with a doctor.

item.title: Restaurant 'admin' fees spark backlash as diners question what they're paying for
item.description: A Florida restaurant owner explains why she avoids admin fees after an Earls Kitchen + Bar surcharge ignited fresh outrage over hidden restaurant costs.
item.content:encoded:
A diner is calling out a restaurant chain over an administrative fee added to his bill, renewing debate over the extra charges that have become increasingly common at restaurants.

The diner visited an Earls Kitchen + Bar in Denver, ordering a $24.75 burger and upgrading to truffle fries for $3, according to a receipt shared on Reddit.

In addition to $2.28 in taxes, the bill included an 83-cent "Admin Fee" — 3% of the food and beverage subtotal — bringing the total to $30.86 before tip.

APPLEBEE'S CUSTOMER PUSHES BACK ON SUGGESTED TIP AFTER CHECKING THE MATH

"What the h--- is even an ‘admin fee’?" the person wrote in the post. "Can a guy even enjoy a burger without being harassed and extorted in this God-forsaken place? This pissed me off. … No tip for you!"

Other Reddit users similarly questioned the charge, with some saying administrative fees would cause them to reduce or eliminate their tips.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Reddit user and Earls for comment.

The controversy comes as restaurants across the country grapple with how to pass along higher costs without alienating increasingly price-conscious customers.

TEXAS BBQ JOINT TAKES DRASTIC STEP AS SOARING BEEF PRICES DEVOUR RESTAURANT

Some operators have turned to administrative, service or operations fees rather than incorporating the additional costs into menu prices — a practice that has generated pushback when diners encounter another charge on the final bill.

In Florida, restaurants have faced new requirements since July 1 aimed at making those charges more transparent.

Under the law, restaurants imposing an "operations charge" must disclose the amount or percentage and its purpose before a customer orders. The law does not prohibit the fees.

But some restaurant owners say the better approach is to skip the fees altogether.

SHAKE SHACK CUSTOMER HITS 'NO TIP' AT KIOSK, THEN WATCHES PRICES JUMP IN VIRAL VIDEO

Vicki Parmelee, owner of Jumby Bay Island Grill in Jupiter, Florida, told Fox News Digital that she prefers incorporating rising expenses into menu prices rather than surprising customers with another charge at the end of a meal.

"I believe in being transparent and giving the customer a choice," Parmelee said.

"I prefer raising the menu prices to reflect real costs and then offering a clear cash or debit discount over adding an 'admin,' 'service' or processing fee that may come as a complete surprise after your meal. People see that as a gotcha, and that last impression is what they remember and share online."

Other restaurant operators appear to be reconsidering the practice.

Florida-based Duffy's Sports Grill previously charged a 3% operations fee. An October state restaurant inspection report for a West Palm Beach location noted the fee and cited the establishment because, while the charge and its purpose were disclosed on the menu, it did not appear properly on the customer's receipt.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Duffy's has since announced that it has ended the fee. Fox News Digital reached out to Duffy's for comment.

Restaurant customers have taken to social media in several states to complain about similarly labeled charges, while operators have defended them, arguing it's necessary to combat rising expenses without increasing menu prices.

Restaurants may turn to additional fees because of the financial pressures they face, Parmelee said.

"Restaurant margins are thin," she said. "Many places have tried an added fee because it feels like the most direct way to offset card costs. The problem is customer reaction — especially when the fee appears only on the final bill."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The charges could also have an unintended consequence for restaurant employees, Parmelee added.

"In my experience, if a restaurant adds an unexpected fee at the end of the meal, people feel nickel-and-dimed and tip less," she said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Restaurants that do impose fees should make them clear before customers order, Parmelee said.

"Guests deserve to understand why the price is what it is and what their choices are," she said. "When it's hidden or comes as a surprise, they don't."

item.title: Prince William has 'learned' to live without Prince Harry as royal feud reaches breaking point: expert
item.description: Prince William has reportedly learned to live without Prince Harry as royal experts say reconciliation now appears past the point of no return.
item.content:encoded:
Prince William has "learned" to live without Prince Harry as their bitter feud appears to have pushed the brothers past the point of no return.

"Harry has never believed he has anything to apologize for," Christopher Andersen, author of "Kate!," told Fox News Digital.

"William had never believed he had anything to apologize for. Reconciliation is not in the cards. It shouldn't come as any surprise that William views Harry as having betrayed not only the royal family but the institution of the monarchy itself. Harry returning to the U.K. and picking up where he left off before Megxit just rubbed salt into an already festering wound."

PRINCE WILLIAM ‘INCANDESCENT WITH ANGER’ AT PRINCE HARRY AS DIANA ANNIVERSARY DEEPENS ROYAL RIFT: PIERS MORGAN

"These are two extraordinarily strong and stubborn men who have, sadly, learned over the past few years that they can live without each other," Andersen said. "If the death of their grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, their father's coronation and the cancer battles of both the king and the Princess of Wales didn't bring them together, it's very hard to imagine what would."

Andersen's comments came after a source told People magazine that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are not planning to apologize to William and his wife, Kate Middleton. The U.K.'s Express previously reported that Harry and Meghan hoped to apologize to the Prince and Princess of Wales over comments made during their 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey as part of an effort to reconcile.

A source close to Harry and Meghan told People that the report was "nonsense."

WATCH HERE: PRINCE HARRY MUST APOLOGIZE TO THE ROYAL FAMILY: AUTHOR

The Express reported that the couple specifically planned to apologize over Meghan's revelation during the televised interview that there had been "concerns and conversations" within the royal family about how dark Prince Archie's skin might be before he was born.

People reported that while Harry has made progress in rebuilding his relationship with his father, King Charles, "there’s no movement, especially on William’s side," said a source.

Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell and Kensington Palace for comment.

British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that William is unlikely to forgive his brother. She noted that William once saw Harry as a supportive "wingman" as he prepared for his future role as king.

"Reportedly, Prince William finds it impossible to forgive his brother for leaving him to cope with the pressure of being future king on his own," Chard said. "The sheer stress and upset caused to his family over the past few years is impossible to forgive."

Harry has publicly said he would like to reconcile with his family. In May 2025, he told the BBC that he would "love reconciliation." In October 2026, he told GQ that "the most important thing is to reconcile. That's the key point."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Royal commentator Meredith Constant told Fox News Digital that after rewatching Harry and Meghan's 2021 interview with Winfrey, she believes the couple has no reason to apologize.

"Harry and Meghan overwhelmingly say positive things about William and Kate," Constant said.

"Meghan calls Kate a 'good person' and admires how she handled the pre-wedding situation when she hurt Meghan's feelings. The couple's issues were two-pronged: a lack of support and understanding from the monarchy and an invisible contract with the U.K. press that allowed for a sustained character assassination of Meghan that, as she says in the interview, raised the threat risk against her."

"With that said, I don't think they'd go back and do an hour-plus television interview again," Constant added.

Constant said that as the future king, William "should lead and take the first step towards reconciliation."

"But, as Harry said, 'reconciliation requires accountability,'" Constant said. "And how can William or Kate take accountability for a problem that they, and the rest of the royal family, wouldn't even acknowledge exists?"

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back from their roles as senior working royals in 2020, citing intrusive British press coverage and a lack of support from the palace. After moving to California that year, they aired their grievances in interviews and documentaries. Harry's 2023 memoir, "Spare," further strained relations with his family.

The couple returned to the U.K. with their children in August 2026 for an extended stay.

Dick Arbiter, a former press secretary to the queen and author of "On Duty with the Royals," told Fox News Digital that Harry should be the one seeking forgiveness, "not the other way around." He said the queen, who died in 2022, was disappointed when her grandson and his wife stepped back from royal duties.

"He had his own reasons to go," Arbiter said. "I think we can all assume why. How is it affecting the rest of the family? Well, it upset his father for obvious reasons. What is more important to the king is his constitutional duty and the survivability of the monarchy as an institution. That comes first."

"He is not going to reconcile with his son as long as his son continues to rubbish the royal family and continues to talk about private meetings," Arbiter said. "This is one of the reasons why the king has had so few meetings with his son, because no sooner is the meeting over and the door has hit Harry in the back, it's all over the American media."

"He's got to be contrite. He's got to apologize and mean it, not the other way around, because he's asking for apologies from his family. And I'm not terribly sure what he wants apologies for."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Some royal commentators had previously hoped that Kate would bring the brothers together as the royal family's peacemaker. However, Andersen said his sources indicated that the Princess of Wales has no desire to get involved.

"Kate is very disappointed with her brother-in-law," Andersen said. "They were once so close, and I think when this all started, she felt she could bring them back together. But to be honest, Harry's attacks on William and the rest of the royal family have, for the most part, made that impossible. I don't think either side has the appetite to go over what has been said in the past."

"It's only Harry who would 'love reconciliation,' not Prince William," British royal expert Hilary Fordwich said. "He remains furious regarding his brother's betrayal, insults and the damage he has wrought upon the family. The impasse is due to both the lack of trust any of the senior royals have in the Sussexes and the lack of apology from them. Without a formal mea culpa, there is no starting point."

Constant said William's next move could determine whether the brothers begin reconciliation talks. As the future king, his decision could send a message about leadership, forgiveness and the possibility of unity within the fractured royal family.

"I'm not sure what the long game is for Will's communications team of putting out information that William won't budge and continues to ice Harry out," Constant said. "After a while, it starts looking petty. But if William does 'extend the olive branch,' as the U.K. press likes to call it, what impact does that have on the story they've been writing for the past six years about the opposing brothers? Who is the villain of the story then?"

item.title: Fake federal agents push seniors to turn savings into gold bars for couriers to collect
item.description: Scammers posing as FTC agents convinced retirees to buy gold bars and hand them to couriers using secret passwords like "tulip" at restaurants.
item.content:encoded:
Scammers posing as federal agents across the country are dispatching couriers armed with secret passwords to collect gold bars from retirees, in some cases draining their life savings.

In Laramie, Wyoming, authorities said an elderly woman doled out about $131,000 in gold to a courier after people posing as Federal Trade Commission agents convinced her that her money was at risk, and pushed her to buy $460,000 in gold, according to the Laramie Boomerang. Police began investigating on Sept. 22.

In that case, a coin shop owner grew suspicious and suspected she was being scammed when police got involved and eventually arrested Jithin Sunny, who was charged with felony theft.

FORMER DISNEY STAR ERIK VON DETTEN SUED FOR ELDER ABUSE AFTER COUPLE POURED $2.1M RETIREMENT SAVINGS INTO GOLD

A Laramie coin shop owner, police and the elderly victim then teamed up to set a trap, borrowing enough one-ounce gold bars from another dealer to stage a photo of her "purchase" and arranging with her credit union to temporarily process a $500,000 transaction to make it look real. On Oct. 2, she agreed to hand off the gold to a courier at a Qdoba restaurant in Laramie.

She and the courier agreed on a password for the handoff, "tulip," and an undercover detective posing as the victim went to the meeting spot in her place.

SCAMMERS ARE COMING FOR YOUR MONEY. HERE’S THE ONE THING YOU MUST NEVER DO

Sunny, a Canadian citizen, claimed to authorities that he was contacted on Instagram by a group promoting a delivery person job in the U.S., under the impression he'd be delivering antiques to wealthy people.

After his arrest, the Canadian man told authorities he didn't know about the scam, saying he'd been instructed to travel to Laramie, pick up a package from someone and hand it off to a second courier.
